_what: Every PolicyEngine analysis whose comparables search is recorded in this repository, keyed by its sources/ directory. Generated by `python -m scorecard_db.comparables index` from the directories themselves; policyengine-app-v2 reads it to check a research entry's comparables record. A listing means the record passed the gate.

comparisons.title: Removing the childcare cliff-edge: impacts and cost of reform
comparisons.sign_convention: positive = yield to the Exchequer (Table 4.2 notes: 'negative = cost to the Exchequer')
comparisons.estimate_label: Static cost of the 30 funded hours, both limits removed, 2027-28
comparisons.cause: The dashboard's Microcosm release draws each family's use of the extended hours with a mean of about 15 of the 30 weekly hours (microcosm#1126, which derives DfE's mean as about 28.5), so the static cost of the 30 hours is about half what fuller use implies. The dashboard's own full-use sensitivity adds £0.60bn in 2027-28 and £0.70bn in 2029-30 (results.json budget.sensitivities.effects_bn.full_30_hour_usage), and its rerun on the first release with the corrected draw (uk-childcare-100k-threshold#8, an uncertified release) gives £1.009bn and £1.215bn for the 30 hours, 26% and 24% above CenTax's central static cost.
